title: Invoices, estimates and printouts still show only the sell price
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Use staging (preferred), or the Tiered Pricing QA site too once the release is deployed there; production is not needed.
  • Note the attached Today picture shows this screen before the release; the steps check that it still works the same way.
  • Sign in as an Admin whose role has 'Settings — Parts', 'See Financial Data', 'Customers — View', 'Customers — Create & Edit', 'Work Orders — Order Parts' and 'Work Order Lines — Create & Edit'.
  • Have a new category for this test, category A, priced by a new matrix for this test, matrix A, with one cost range ($0.00 and up) whose Default rule is Markup % 35.
  • Have a new tier for this test, tier A, with a name no other tier uses, whose column in matrix A is % Off 10.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer A, put on tier A for work orders in Edit Customer.
  • Have a new work order for this test, work order 1, for customer A, made after customer A's tier was set, with one labor line (line 1) and a tier-priced part in category A at $121.50 and a part with a typed price of $99.00.
  • Use a desktop browser window at least 1440 pixels wide, at 100% zoom, so every column of the page shows.
custom_steps:
1. Open work order 1.
  2. Print the work order.
  3. Open the estimate PDF.
  4. Click Invoice.
  5. Open the invoice PDF.
  6. Open the work order in the customer portal.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Work order 1 opens on its Lines tab.

Step 2:

  • The printout shows the parts at $121.50 and $99.00.
  • It shows no tier name, "Manual", Priced by or price details.

Step 3:

  • The estimate PDF shows the same two sell prices.
  • It names no tier.

Step 4:

  • The invoice is created.

Step 5:

  • The invoice PDF shows $121.50 and $99.00 ($121.50 + $99.00 = $220.50 parts).
  • It names no tier.

Step 6:

  • The portal shows the sell prices.
  • It shows no pricing source.
